name: Spain
headline: Spain: +2.6% growth in 2025, 2.7% inflation, debt 101% of GDP
sections: Spain is a $1.91 trillion economy (2025), the world's 13th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.6% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $60K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 10.6% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.7% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 10.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 24.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 101% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 119% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.4% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +3.2% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 69% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 89% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.9 years (2024). Population: 49.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
